caseno: First Miscellaneous Appeal No. 66 of 2020 with Civil Rule No. 515(FM) of 2018.
lawyer:
HM Barhan, Advocate —For the Appellant. 
Hosneara Begum, Advocate --For the Respondents.
parties:
Anisur Rahman (Md) ------- Judgment Debtor-Appellant
VS
Regional Manager, Bangladesh House Building Finance Corporation, Regional Office, Kushtia Decree Holder-Respondent
Alea Ahmed and others ------ Added Respondents
full_judgment:
Mohi Uddin Shamim, J: This miscellaneous appeal is directed against the order No. 58 dated 11-9-2018 passed by the learned District Judge, Kushtia in Miscellaneous Execution Case No. 1 of 2012, rejecting an application praying for installments in paying the decretal amount filed by the judgment-debtor. 

 2. The facts of the case, in short, are that, the appellant took loan amounting to Taka 5,50,000 from the respondent No. 1, the House Building Finance Corporation, Regional Office, Kushtia on 28-11-1983 for erecting a house. Subsequently, the appellant did not repay the loan. Therefore, the respondent No. 1-Corporation filed a case being Miscellaneous Case No. 77 of 2002 in the Court of District Judge, Kushtia against the appellant for realization of loan along with interest amounting to Taka 17,04,013.49 under the provision of President's Order No. 7 of 1973. After hearing, the said miscellaneous case was decreed by judgment and decree dated 4-10-2010. Thereafter, the respondent No. 1 Corporation filed Miscellaneous Case No. 1 of 2012 for execution of the decree. 

 3. During pendency of the execution case, on 11-7-2018 the judgment-debtor appellant filed an application before the Executing Court praying for 170 monthly installments of Taka 10,024 each in paying the decretal amount. 

 5. Being aggrieved by and dissatisfied with the impugned order, the judgment-debtor, as appellant, has preferred the instant miscellaneous appeal before this Court. 

 6. Mr HM Borhan, the learned Advocate for the appellant, takes us through the Memo of appeal, the impugned order and the other connected materials on record and submits that the appellant is a bonafide borrower of the respondent No. 1 and he paid a reasonable amount towards the outstanding dues, but the respondent-Corporation without adjusting the same and also by imposing the interest beyond the terms of 'loan sanction letter' purposely filed the execution case claiming an unreasonable interest. He next submits that admittedly, the appellant is physically disabled person and due to his physical disability, he could not adjust loan money in time in terms of the loan sanction letter at a time. In such view of the matter, if he had been allowed to pay the loan money in installments, he would repay the decretal amount. He further submits that the learned District Judge has failed to appreciate the application for installment and also to appreciate the physical disability of the appellant in passing the impugned order. He finally submits that the learned District Judge has passed the impugned order on the basis of surmise and conjecture and, as such, the impugned order if liable to set-aside. 

 7. On the contrary Ms. Hosneara Begum, the learned Advocate for the respondent No. 1 Corporation, by filing counter-affidavit and supplementary counter-affidavit contends that, the appellant is a habitual defaulter. He took the instant loan in the year 1983, but he did not repay the same. She next contends that, had the appellant any bonafide intention to repay the loan, he would have repaid the loan during pendency of the miscellaneous case filed by the Corporation for realization of the loan, but did not do so by showing his bonafideness. Moreover, these so-called installments could have been sought for during pendency of the miscellaneous case and the Trial Court was competent to pass a decree on that line basing on the materials on record, but there is no scope to entertain such kind of application at the execution stage. She also contends that after long pursuance when the respondent-Corporation is going to have the decretal amount through execution, then the judgment-debtor as appellant has come with a plea of installments to frustrate the decree. The learned counsel goes on to contend that, considering all the aspects of the case and the conduct of the appellant as regards to payment of the loan, the learned Judge of the Executing Court has rightly rejected the application for installments filed by the appellant and, as such, there is no scope to interfere with the impugned order and finally prays that the instant appeal has got no merit and it is liable to be dismissed. 

 9. Admittedly, the appellant took loan from the respondent No.1-Corporation for erecting house in the year 1983. Thereafter, he did not repay that loan as per terms and condition so set out in the sanction letter. The respondent-Corporation being failed to realize the loan money from the appellant, it then filed the Miscellaneous Case in the concerned competent Court. Ultimately, the said case was decreed in favour of the respondent Corporation. When the said decree was put in execution before the Executing Court, then the judgment-debtor appellant came with a plea of installments in repaying the decretal amount. We have already seen that, the conduct of the judgment-debtor appellant was not satisfactory in dealing with repayment of loan. Considering the facts and circumstance of the case and also considering the conduct of the judgment-debtor appellant as regards to non-payment of the loan since long, we are of the view that if the installments as prayed for by the appellant is allowed at this stage, there is least chance of realization of the decretal amount. The learned Judge of the Executing Court also considering all these aspect of the case has rightly rejected the application for installment filed on behalf of the judgment-debtor appellant by the impugned order. Therefore, the impugned order does not call for any interference by this Court. 

 10. Further, the appellant did not pray for any installment to repay the loan money before the Trial Court in the miscellaneous case. He filed the application for installment before the Executing Court, which is beyond its jurisdiction. Save and except the execution of the decree, the Execution Court has got no authority to grant such installments through alteration or modification of the decree. It has only authority to execute a decree as it is and no way it can go beyond the decree. 

 14. The order of stay as granted by this Court in Civil Rule No. 515(fm) of 2018 as regards to further proceedings of the Execution Case stands vacated.
